narrative: The model estimated a 51.0% chance that you will fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is only slightly above even odds and does not mean failure is certain, but it was enough for the admissions process to treat bar-exam success as too uncertain and deny your application. The strongest influence was your third-year class rank: you are in the lowest decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile. This was the main factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.70 was the next most important factor, and because it is well above the accepted-student average of 3.23, it pushed toward passing and worked in your favor. Your LSAT score was the third-most influential factor and contributed a smaller amount toward passing. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction. To move forward, ask admissions whether the decision can be reviewed and explain any circumstances behind your third-year ranking. Ask what evidence would strengthen your case, such as improved academic performance, a realistic bar-preparation plan, or, if feasible, a stronger LSAT retake. Because the estimate is close to 50%, the decision may be sensitive to new information, so a clear, documented appeal or updated application is worthwhile.
